To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the expression of a large number of genes is age‐dependent, and that the expression of many of these changes in an invariant manner.

the expression of a subset of genes in the adult fly undergoes a dynamic and age‐dependent regulation, that the expression of these genes is under the control of a small number of transcription factors, and that the regulation of the expression of the genes is important for the maintenance of the adult life of the fly.

the expression of many Drosophila genes changes with age and that these age‐dependent changes are often correlated with the life‐expectancy of the gene product and the function of the encoded protein.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular genetics of aging in Drosophila.
identifying genes and gene products that affect the rate of aging.
the molecular mechanisms underlying life span determination in Drosophila and how this relates to the biology of the aging process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the genetic analysis of aging in the fruit fly Drosophila melanogaster has provided a wealth of information that is beginning to challenge many of the commonly held assumptions about aging and has provided new insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying aging.
we do not know how we age and that we do not have any good theories on the process of aging.
the fly has provided a wealth of information that has helped to shape the field of aging research and will continue to be of great importance in the future.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have been able to demonstrate that the aging of the adult Drosophila melanogaster is a highly dynamic and well‐regulated process.
we have identified a number of genes and molecular pathways that are involved in aging and have begun to understand how they function.
we have shown that the molecular life of Drosophila is a period of dynamic, well‐regulated change and that the fly is a good model for the study of aging.
The main takeaway from our work is that
aging is not a passive decline but a dynamic process that involves changes in gene expression.
aging is a complex phenomenon and that the molecular mechanisms underlying aging may differ between organisms.
aging is not a passive process, but rather one of dynamic change.
